Wizard_Language.T: SelfX package wizard

Default language of SelfX on the devices (de, en, fr, es ... or Auto)
Auto follows the display language of Windows. Choose Auto if your users speak several languages.
May users choose their language in the settings?
Yes. It costs nothing and helps multilingual staff.
Name of your organisation (used for the Intune app name and the instructions)
The short name of your company or authority, for example Contoso.
Name of the tool in the title bar and the shortcuts
Keep SelfX. Users find it faster when the name is the same everywhere.
For which Windows is this package? Windows11 (PCs and notebooks, installed with Intune) or WindowsServer (Windows Server 2022 or 2025 as a terminal server, installed without Intune)

Windows11 for PCs and notebooks. WindowsServer for terminal servers: there SelfX hides actions and repairs that affect the whole server or all users, and the service refuses them. SelfX takes this from Windows itself; the answer chooses the instructions at the end (Intune cannot install apps on Windows Server) and the question about the device status.
Device status on the terminal server: Off (nobody) or AdminOnly (only administrators who started SelfX with elevated rights)

Off. On a terminal server the device status shows the server (updates, Defender, restart), not the place of work of the user, and users could not fix it. Choose AdminOnly when your administrators want to use it.
Greeting in the SelfX window: FirstName ("Good morning, Anna." with the first name that Windows knows for the account) or Off (always "Welcome.")

FirstName. Without a first name, or when the Windows privacy setting "Account info" does not allow it, SelfX greets without a name; it never takes the display name or the account name instead. The name is not logged, saved or sent anywhere.
Support e-mail address (shared mailbox)
Use a shared (functional) mailbox, never a personal one. The address is also the recipient of the device logs e-mail.
Fixed support e-mail address for the terminal server (support e-mail, ticket and help window)

The address of the team that supports the terminal server. On Windows Server it replaces the support e-mail and the ticket recipient, and the routing to support units is not used (it describes devices of one person). The computer name of the server stays in the ticket.
Support phone number (empty = hide)
Enter a number only if somebody answers it during the support hours.
Support hours (empty = hide)
For example Mon-Fri 08:00-17:00.
Support website or ticket portal (https://, empty = hide)
Enter your self-service portal if you have one. Only https:// addresses are accepted.
Teams contact (address of a shared account or https:// link, empty = hide)
Optional. Leave it empty if the Service Desk is not reachable in Teams.
Path of your logo file (png, jpg or ico, at most 2 MB, empty = no logo)
A transparent PNG, about 400 x 120 pixels, looks good in the light and the dark design.
Company color as #RRGGBB (empty = keep SelfX blue #0072BC)
Use your corporate color. SelfX adjusts colors that are too dark or too light.
Do you want the ticket function (the user describes the problem, SelfX opens a prepared e-mail)?
Yes, if your Service Desk accepts tickets by e-mail. The user always checks and sends the e-mail; SelfX sends nothing itself.
Default recipient of ticket e-mails
Your Service Desk mailbox. It is used when no organisation rule matches.
Marker at the start of the subject line (for mail filters)
Keep SelfX, or use a short tag your ticket system filters on. Up to 20 characters: letters, digits . _ -
Do tickets of other organisations or locations have to go to other mailboxes?
Answer yes if several IT units are responsible for different devices. You then define one unit per mailbox.
Are devices hybrid joined (Active Directory)? Then SelfX can route by OU.
Yes, if your devices are in an on-premises domain. Cloud-only (Entra joined) devices have no OU.
Do you route by the Autopilot group tag (Entra ID)?
Yes, if your Autopilot devices carry a group tag per organisation. It is the most reliable criterion for cloud-only devices.
Do you route by device class (notebook, PC, tablet)?
Yes, if another team handles tablets or kiosk PCs. SelfX runs on Windows 11 only: smartphones (iOS, Android) cannot be covered by SelfX.
Organisation / unit {0}
Short name of the unit (letters, digits . _ -)
For example IT-Berlin. The name is only used inside the configuration.
Mailbox of this unit
One plain address, shared mailbox only. The file Ticket_Config.xml can be read by every user on the device. Addresses that must stay hidden belong into the per-device registry value TicketMail.
Copy (Cc) of this unit (empty = none)
Optional second shared mailbox.
Autopilot group tags of this unit (comma separated)
Exactly as in Entra ID, for example DE-IT1-BER. Letters, digits, space . _ - up to 64 characters.
OU names of this unit (comma separated)
Part of the distinguished name, for example OU=Berlin. SelfX searches it in the OU of the computer account.
Device classes of this unit (comma separated)
Free names such as Notebook, Desktop, Tablet. Intune sets the value per device group.
Add another unit?
Yes until every mailbox is defined. The first matching rule wins: group tags are checked first, then OUs, then device classes.
Do you want the connection check (WLAN, internet, Microsoft services, company network) in the system information?

Yes, if users should see at once whether the router, the internet or the company network is the problem. SelfX only tests whether a connection can be opened and sends no data. The check is off in the delivered file.
Test the Microsoft services for Intune and Entra ID too?
Yes uses the four endpoints that are delivered in Network_Test_Config.xml (Intune service, Entra ID sign-in and directory, device registration). Answer no if your firewall blocks them on purpose.
Show the host names of the targets in the support report and in the ticket?
No hides internal host names there: the report then shows only the label of a target. The window of the user always shows the labels.
Do you want to add your own network targets (for example the VPN gateway or an intranet server)?
The users cannot change or add targets. At most 12 targets are possible in total, the four delivered Microsoft targets included (so 8 own ones).
Network target {0}
Name of the target (shown to the user)
For example VPN gateway. Letters, digits, space . _ - up to 40 characters. Do not use a secret name.
Host name or IPv4 address
Only the name, for example vpn.contoso.example. No https://, no path, no port. The file Network_Test_Config.xml can be read by every user on the device.
TCP port (0 = only look up the name)
For example 443 or 445. An IPv4 address needs a port.
What does the target show?
Local = your own router or printer, Internet = a public site, Microsoft = a Microsoft service, Company = the company network (VPN or intranet).
Kind of the company target
Vpn = reachable only after the VPN is connected: SelfX then says "check the VPN". Intranet = reachable in the office network. None = no statement.
Add another target?
Yes until every target is defined.
Do you have Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat licensed and want to offer it in the help dialog?
Yes if your users have Copilot Chat. SelfX uses no interface and no token: it prepares a text, the user pastes it into Copilot.
Do you want a button that opens the wiki or intranet page of your company in the web browser?
Yes if you have a wiki with tips and tricks for your staff. The button is shown in the navigation of SelfX.
Address of the wiki (https://)
The page that opens on a click, for example https://wiki.contoso.example. Only https:// is accepted.
Name on the button (empty = Company wiki, up to 40 characters)
Optional, for example Contoso Wiki. Empty shows a text in the language of the user.
Who is the answer for? User (plain language) or Admin (technical steps)
User. Technical answers confuse most employees.
Empty the clipboard a few minutes after SelfX copied the text?
Yes if the text should not stay in the clipboard. The text already contains no names or addresses.
Show the status icon next to the clock for all users?
Yes. Users see problems early and open SelfX with one click.
Before an action that can interrupt a meeting (closing Teams or Office, restarting the network or the device): show a hint when the user appears to be presenting or in full screen?
Yes. It is only a sentence in the confirmation; nothing is blocked or switched. Windows tells SelfX only about presentation mode, full screen and quiet time, so not every meeting is recognised.
Intune Remediations: copy a detection script into the output folder that shows the SelfX device status of every Windows 11 device in Intune (one line per device, "with issues" on an error)?
No, unless you use Intune Remediations (it needs Windows Enterprise E3 or E5 or a similar license). No remediation script is needed: the script only reads the status of SelfX and changes nothing.
Inventory file: shall the SelfX service write the device status after every check as one JSON line to %ProgramData%\SelfX\Inventory, for a log collector such as the Azure Monitor Agent?
No, unless a collector reads the file (Log Analytics, see docs\Monitoring.md). The file has no names and no detail texts; on Windows Server nothing is written while the device status is off.
Create a shortcut on the public desktop?
Yes for the start, so that users find SelfX. Switch it off later if desktops should stay empty.
Create a shortcut in the Start menu?
Yes.
Do you want to change security and log settings (expert)?
No. The secure defaults stay: the service starts nothing when files do not match (Enforce) and runs with reduced rights (Restricted).
Days to keep log files (1-3650)
90 days is a good balance between support needs and data minimisation.
File check of the service: Enforce or Audit
Enforce. Audit only reports and is meant for a short pilot.
Rights of the service: Restricted or Default
Restricted. Default is only for troubleshooting.
Create AppLocker rules for the programs of SelfX?
Yes if you use AppLocker. The file SelfX.AppLocker.xml has hash rules (signed package: one publisher rule that stays the same for every version). Answer no if this PC has no AppLocker cmdlets.
Base policy ID (GUID) of your App Control for Business (WDAC) policy (empty = no App Control file)
Only if you use App Control. The assistant then creates a supplemental policy for this base policy. It needs Windows 11 with the ConfigCI module and takes a few minutes. Empty creates nothing.
Path of IntuneWinAppUtil.exe (Win32 Content Prep Tool of Microsoft)
Download it from https://github.com/microsoft/Microsoft-Win32-Content-Prep-Tool (file IntuneWinAppUtil.exe in the repository, use the latest release tag). The script checks the Microsoft signature.
The programs (folder Bin) are missing or outdated. Build them now with the .NET SDK 10?
Yes. The build needs the .NET SDK 10 but no internet: the packages come from the folder offline-feed.
Output folder
The folder receives the package, the detection script, the scripts for Intune and the instructions. Do not commit it.
Summary of your answers
Create the package with these settings?
Yes, if the summary is correct. Nothing is installed or sent; the package is only built.

Defender attack surface reduction (only if the rule "Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion", ID 01443614-cd74-433a-b99e-2ecdc07bfc25, is active in your tenant): the cloud protection of Microsoft decides which programs may start and you cannot set its criteria, so a program of SelfX may be blocked. This is possible, not certain: check it on the pilot devices before you widen the assignment.

Which file is blocked? Copy tools\Get-SelfXAsrEvents.ps1 from the repository to a pilot device and run it there (read only, no user names in the output, add -SelfXOnly for the SelfX files; run it elevated if the log cannot be read). Event 1121 = blocked, 1122 = only recorded in audit mode.

Set the rule to Audit mode first. If the events name SelfX files, add exactly these files (never more than the following five) to the setting "ASR Only Per Rule Exclusions" of this rule: Endpoint security > Attack surface reduction > your policy of the type Attack surface reduction rules.

Do not exclude the folder SelfX and do not use the global setting "Attack Surface Reduction Only Exclusions" (it applies to every ASR rule). An exclusion applies when the program starts: restart the service SelfXService or the device. Excluded files write no events. Signing the package is no guarantee that the rule lets the files pass. Details: docs\Installation.md, section "Defender ASR: rule for executable files".

If the signature is not accepted on a device, the service starts nothing: event 4006 (trust anchor missing or unsafe) or 4007 (a script, a library or a catalog has no valid signature of an allowed signer) in the Application log; SelfXService.log names the file and the reason (docs\Installation.md, Troubleshooting).

Change of the signing certificate (renewal or new certificate): 1) build the package again with the old certificate and add the thumbprint of the new one as an additional signer, roll it out; 2) when all devices have it, build with the new certificate (the old thumbprint can stay as an additional signer for a while); 3) later build without the old thumbprint.
Devices accept only signers named in -TrustedSigner of their last installation. A package signed with a certificate the devices do not know yet is refused.

Use a time stamp service: without a time stamp the signatures become invalid when the certificate expires, and the service starts nothing (it notices an expired or revoked certificate after 60 minutes at the latest).

AppLocker and App Control: a renewed certificate with the same subject needs no new rules; with another subject create the publisher rules again before the first package with the new certificate. Details: docs\Certificate-Guide.md.
